core: 作为 introduces the role, identity, or viewpoint from which someone speaks or acts. Learners often overuse it for everyday comparisons, while natives reserve it for framing identity, duty, or perspective.

collocations.pinyin: zuò wéi shēng rì lǐ wù

sentences.situation: At a café · to your close friend
sentences.zh: 作为朋友，我得提醒你这件事不太合适。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi péng yǒu, wǒ děi tí xǐng nǐ zhè jiàn shì bú tài hé shì.
sentences.en: As a friend, I have to remind you this is not very appropriate.
sentences.why: You use this when you want to give honest advice without sounding judgmental. It signals you are speaking from a caring, equal friend perspective.
sentences.tip: Do not overuse 作为 with close friends; it sounds slightly formal if you say it too often.

sentences.situation: At home · to your younger sibling
sentences.zh: 作为哥哥，我会帮你解决这个问题。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi gē ge, wǒ huì bāng nǐ jiě jué zhè ge wèn tí.
sentences.en: As an older brother, I will help you solve this problem.
sentences.why: You frame your duty using your family role. It sounds responsible and warm, especially with younger family members.
sentences.tip: Change 哥哥 to 姐姐, 爸爸, or 妈妈 depending on your role.

sentences.situation: At a gift shop · to your colleague
sentences.zh: 这个杯子可以作为出差带回来的纪念品。
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge bēi zi kě yǐ zuò wéi chū chāi dài huí lái de jì niàn pǐn.
sentences.en: This cup can serve as a souvenir from your business trip.
sentences.why: Here 作为 means to function as something. You are suggesting a suitable use for an object.
sentences.tip: This pattern is common when choosing small gifts or keepsakes.

sentences.situation: At work · to your direct manager
sentences.zh: 作为员工，我完全理解公司的决定。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi yuán gōng, wǒ wán quán lǐ jiě gōng sī de jué dìng.
sentences.en: As an employee, I fully understand the company's decision.
sentences.why: You acknowledge your position in the company before stating your attitude. It shows professionalism and alignment with workplace expectations.
sentences.tip: Saying this to your boss is safe and polite, but do not use it with peers unless you want to sound formal.

sentences.situation: During a team meeting · presenting to clients
sentences.zh: 作为项目负责人，我想先介绍一下我们的方案。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi xiàng mù fù zé rén, wǒ xiǎng xiān jiè shào yí xià wǒ men de fāng àn.
sentences.en: As the project lead, I would like to first introduce our proposal.
sentences.why: You establish your authority and role before speaking in a professional setting. This is standard in meetings or presentations.
sentences.tip: Natives often use 作为 + job title at the start of formal remarks.

sentences.situation: At a restaurant · with a close friend
sentences.zh: 作为吃货，这家新开的火锅店我一定要去试试。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi chī huò, zhè jiā xīn kāi de huǒ guō diàn wǒ yí dìng yào qù shì shi.
sentences.en: As a foodie, I definitely have to try this new hot pot restaurant.
sentences.why: You use 作为 humorously with a self-given identity, like being a foodie. It is a light way to justify strong preferences.
sentences.tip: 吃货 is a casual, fun word; avoid it in very formal settings.

sentences.zh: 这张照片可以作为我们毕业旅行的纪念。
sentences.pinyin: zhè zhāng zhào piàn kě yǐ zuò wéi wǒ men bì yè lǚ xíng de jì niàn.
sentences.en: This photo can serve as a memento of our graduation trip.
sentences.why: You are suggesting an object or moment as a keepsake. It carries emotional value in personal relationships.
sentences.tip: When sending photos, natives often say 留作纪念 instead of 作为纪念.

sentences.situation: At work · to your team member
sentences.zh: 作为同事，我觉得你应该和领导直接沟通这件事。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi tóng shì, wǒ jué de nǐ yīng gāi hé lǐng dǎo zhí jiē gōu tōng zhè jiàn shì.
sentences.en: As a colleague, I think you should communicate this directly with the manager.
sentences.why: You are giving advice while clarifying you are speaking from a peer perspective, not as their boss.
sentences.tip: This softens advice so it does not sound like you are ordering them around.

sentences.situation: At a company annual meeting · formal speech
sentences.zh: 作为公司的老员工，我亲眼见证了这五年的成长。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi gōng sī de lǎo yuán gōng, wǒ qīn yǎn jiàn zhèng le zhè wǔ nián de chéng zhǎng.
sentences.en: As a long-time employee, I have personally witnessed the growth over these five years.
sentences.why: This is typical in speeches where someone shares history and loyalty. It builds trust with the audience.
sentences.tip: 老员工 means experienced or long-serving staff, not literally old age.

sentences.situation: At home · comforting your child before exams
sentences.zh: 作为父母，我们不要求你考满分，只要你尽力就好。
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi fù mǔ, wǒ men bù yāo qiú nǐ kǎo mǎn fēn, zhǐ yào nǐ jìn lì jiù hǎo.
sentences.en: As your parents, we do not expect you to get full marks; as long as you try your best, it is enough.
sentences.why: Parents use this to reduce pressure while expressing unconditional support. It frames expectations from a loving family role.
sentences.tip: The pause after 作为父母 makes the sentence sound warm and deliberate.

quiz.prompt: Tell your friend that as a friend, you want to give them honest advice about their new job.
quiz.answer: 作为朋友，我想跟你说句实在话，这份新工作可能不太适合你。
accept: 作为朋友，我得提醒你，这份新工作要多考虑一下。
作为朋友，我建议你再想想这份新工作。
quiz.explain: Starting with 作为朋友 softens honest advice and shows you care.

quiz.prompt: Say that this small gift can be used as a souvenir from your trip.
quiz.answer: 这个小礼物可以作为这次旅行的纪念品。
accept: 这个小礼物可以作为旅行的纪念。
这个小礼物可以留作旅行纪念。
quiz.explain: 作为 + souvenir phrase is the natural way to say something serves as a keepsake.

quiz.prompt: Politely tell your manager that as a team leader, you take responsibility for the project delay.
quiz.answer: 作为团队负责人，这次项目延期的责任主要在我。
accept: 作为团队负责人，我会为这次项目延期负责。
作为项目负责人，这次延期我有责任。
quiz.explain: Using your role before taking responsibility sounds professional and mature.

quiz.prompt: Jokingly tell your friend that as a coffee lover, you have to try every new café in the city.
quiz.answer: 作为咖啡爱好者，这家新开的咖啡馆我一定要去试试。
accept: 作为咖啡爱好者，我得去试试这家新开的咖啡馆。
作为爱喝咖啡的人，这家新店我肯定要去打卡。
quiz.explain: 作为 + personal identity is a fun way to justify a hobby or preference.

quiz.prompt: 你的朋友问你：你为什么这么支持这家小书店？ 请用作为回答。
quiz.answer: 作为顾客，我觉得这家书店的氛围很好，所以愿意一直支持它。
accept: 作为常来的客人，我很喜欢这家书店，所以会一直支持。
作为读者，我觉得这家书店很用心，所以愿意支持它。
quiz.explain: You explain your viewpoint from your identity as a customer or reader.

quiz.prompt: 同事问你：这次活动你为什么愿意帮忙？ 请用作为回答。
quiz.answer: 作为团队的一员，大家的事就是我的事，当然愿意帮忙。
accept: 作为团队的一员，我觉得帮忙是应该的。
作为这个团队的人，大家的活动我当然要支持。
quiz.explain: Using 作为团队的一员 frames your willingness to help as part of group responsibility.
